sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The envelope check is incomplete: MIN(?intendedY) considers only intended-waterline points that happen to exist at exactly ?x, so an intended waterline missing that station is silently excluded, and crossings or lower segments between represented points can pass even when the LIWL is not the pointwise lower envelope. Repair the bounded envelope validation so every comparison station has a value from every intended ice-operating waterline and the broken-line geometry includes all relevant vertices/intersections, then compare the LIWL value with the minimum using tolerance scaled from that expected minimum. Preserve the reverse check preventing unsupported LIWL stations; no vocabulary matcher is needed.

The prior envelope repair remains incomplete. Both queries use only explicitly stored profile-point x-coordinates and require exact points on every waterline at each such x; they neither interpolate the broken-line segments nor derive and check relevant segment intersections where the lowest intended waterline can change. This can reject valid unsynchronized broken-line representations and can accept an LIWL that matches sampled vertices but is not the pointwise lower envelope between them. Repair the bounded geometry check to evaluate each intended waterline and the LIWL by linear interpolation on the segment containing each comparison x, include all profile vertices and relevant in-range segment-intersection x-coordinates, require a defined value from every intended waterline and the LIWL at each comparison station, and compare the LIWL value to the minimum intended value using tolerance scaled from that expected minimum. Preserve the reverse coverage check so unsupported LIWL portions cannot pass. No vocabulary matcher is needed.

The revised interpolation covers profile vertices and relevant intended-waterline intersections, enforces station coverage, and scales tolerance from the expected minimum, but it implements the envelope through two large SPARQL constraints with duplicated combinatorial station-generation logic. Consolidate this into one bounded formula SPARQL constraint, leaving structural cardinality, class, datatype, and unit checks in SHACL Core. The unified query must generate the finite comparison-station set once and report a violation if any intended waterline or LIWL lacks an interpolated value there, or if the LIWL differs from the minimum intended value beyond the existing expected-value-scaled tolerance. Preserve all vertex/intersection stations and the reverse coverage of LIWL-only portions. No vocabulary matcher is needed.

Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Embedded SHACL-SPARQL nests OPTIONAL inside FILTER NOT EXISTS; use SHACL Core for required fields and a bounded positive formula pattern
Semantic validator feedback: deterministicValidation.valid is false because the embedded SHACL-SPARQL contains the prohibited non-portable OPTIONAL/FILTER NOT EXISTS nesting. Refactor required profile-point, coordinate, datatype, unit, and cardinality checks into SHACL Core, and retain only one bounded positive formula constraint for the envelope calculation without OPTIONAL nested in FILTER NOT EXISTS or duplicated/combinatorial station-generation logic. Preserve all prior requirements: generate the finite station set once from intended and LIWL vertices plus relevant in-range intended-segment intersections; interpolate every intended waterline and the LIWL at each station; fail when any required value is undefined, including LIWL-only unsupported portions; and compare the LIWL against the pointwise intended minimum using tolerance scaled from that expected minimum. No vocabulary matcher is needed.

Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Embedded SHACL-SPARQL nests OPTIONAL inside FILTER NOT EXISTS; use SHACL Core for required fields and a bounded positive formula pattern
Semantic validator feedback: Deterministic validation is still invalid: the envelope query places FILTER NOT EXISTS inside OPTIONAL blocks and remains non-portable and prone to accidental passes. Refactor the structural existence, class, coordinate, datatype, unit, and cardinality requirements into SHACL Core, and retain one bounded positive SPARQL formula constraint without OPTIONAL/FILTER NOT EXISTS nesting or duplicated/combinatorial segment discovery. Preserve all prior semantic requirements: generate the finite comparison-station set once from intended-waterline and LIWL vertices plus relevant in-range intended-segment intersections; interpolate every intended waterline and the LIWL at every station; report missing interpolated values, including unsupported LIWL-only portions; and compare the LIWL with the minimum intended value using tolerance scaled from that expected minimum. No vocabulary matcher is needed.
